content: Econazole is a topical medication prescribed to treat various skin infections, including athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. In some cases, it may be used for other conditions as determined by your doctor. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Econazole is available as a cream that is applied directly to the skin. It is typically used once or twice daily, in the morning and evening, for a duration of two weeks. However, certain infections may require treatment for up to six weeks. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not apply more or less than prescribed, and do not use it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Before applying the cream, thoroughly clean the affected area and allow it to dry. Gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it is absorbed. Use only enough cream to cover the infected area. After application, wash your hands to prevent the spread of infection. Continue using econazole even if your symptoms improve. Do not stop using the medication without consulting your doctor. Before starting econazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to econazole or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription drugs, including vitamins, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using econazole, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Econazole may cause side effects. If you experience itching, burning, irritation, stinging, redness, or a rash, contact your doctor immediately. If you experience a severe reaction, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store econazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Econazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes or mouth, and do not swallow the medication. Do not apply cosmetics, lotions, or other skin products to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, ask your pharmacist. If your symptoms persist after completing the treatment, contact your doctor.
